key_insight: Equal-weight 6H-SiC/h-BN composites combine stability under oxidizing exposure above 1500 °C with unusually temperature-independent thermal conductivity.
engineering_relevance: This lightweight, machinable ceramic is a promising candidate for structural components exposed to extreme heat, oxidation, and thermal cycling.
method: Spark plasma sintering of equal-weight 6H-SiC and h-BN.
High-velocity oxygen-fuel torch testing and microstructural evaluation.
Finite-element thermal analysis and ReaxFF molecular dynamics.
evidence_signal: Torch tests showed prolonged heating and thermal-cycling survival above 1500 °C, while pure constituents rapidly fractured or eroded; microscopy identified a protective multiphase silica surface layer.
watch_item: The abstract does not quantify exposure duration, cycle count, or retained mechanical strength, limiting service-life assessment.
paper_title: SiC-BN composites with extreme thermal and environmental stability
